title: Beginning Basketball
description: Exercise and Nutritional Sciences 108.

title: Beginning Volleyball
description: Exercise and Nutritional Sciences 110.

title: Beginning Tennis
description: An introduction to basic rules, terminology, fundamentals, and etiquette in tennis, providing knowledge and instruction to confidently play tennis as a fitness and leisure activity and applying sports terminology and rules to standard match play and skill-enhancing drills.

title: Intermediate Tennis
description: Provides additional knowledge and instruction to play with greater confidence for fitness and/or leisure. Students will identify proper tennis sports terminology and rules and apply these concepts in standard match play and skill-enhancing drills

title: Beginning Bowling
description: Beginning Bowling.

title: Intermediate Bowling
description: Intermediate Bowling.

title: Mission Bay Aquatic Center Selected Activities
description: May be repeated with new activity.

title: Selected Activities
description: May be repeated with new activity for additional credit.

title: Beginning Rock Climbing
description: Rock climbing concepts and theories. Active participation using beginning techniques and training concepts.

title: Intermediate Rock Climbing
description: Rock climbing concepts and theories. Active participation using advanced techniques, training concepts, and lead climbing concepts expected.

title: Introduction to Exercise and Nutritional Sciences
description: Overview of disciplines of kinesiology and foods and nutrition. Current and emerging issues, ethical considerations, and professional practice.

title: Medical Terminology
description: Comprehensive introduction to the medical terminology used in health care. Learn the Greek and Latin words used to describe the body systems as well as equipment, diagnoses, and treatment.
notes: Open to all majors. Not open to students with credit in BIOL 277.

title: Physical Education of Children
description: Physical education of elementary school-aged children: Theory and activity.
notes: Not open to students with credit in ENS 241A and ENS 241B. Not open to Kinesiology majors.

title: Care and Prevention of Athletic and Recreational Injuries
description: Mechanisms of common sports injuries, acute care of injuries, risk management and prevention of injuries, psychosocial intervention and referral, and basic health care administration.

title: Care and Prevention of Athletic and Recreational Injuries Laboratory
description: Students will learn mechanisms of common sports injuries, acute care of injuries, risk management and prevention of injuries, psychosocial intervention and referral, and basic administration of athletic training skills.
notes: The following student levels are not allowed: Graduate.

title: Experimental Topics
description: Selected topics.
notes: See Class Schedule for specific content. Limit of nine units of any combination of 296, 496, 596 courses applicable to a bachelor’s degree.

title: Special Study
description: Individual study.

title: Applied Kinesiology
description: Arthrology, syndesmology and myology, with emphasis on movement analysis. Muscle groups and their functional relationships. Application of simple mechanical principles to movement analysis.

title: Physiology of Exercise
description: Effects of physical activities on physiological functions of the body.

title: Exercise Physiology Laboratory
description: Laboratory experiences in the application of exercises and the analysis of the results.

title: Measurement and Evaluation in Kinesiology
description: Testing and measurement for assessment and understanding of physical performance and for planning and evaluation of instruction in physical activity settings. Planning, implementation, and evaluation of tests.

title: Biomechanics of Human Movement
description: Mechanical principles as applied to movement; analysis and application to selected motor skills.

title: Neuroscience of Movement
description: Neural structures and processes involved in movement production and movement disorders.

title: Biomechanics Foundations
description: Foundational physics concepts in biomechanics for students without a prior physics course.

title: Adaptive Sports and Fitness
description: Adaptive sports and fitness with emphasis on historical development, practical applications, and contemporary issues in inclusivity and accessibility.

title: Sport, Games, and Culture
description: Contemporary games and sports. Anthro-historical development of sports and philosophies, political economies, and socio-cultural influences. Psychological performance modalities of modern sport.

title: Applied Assessments in Health and Fitness
description: Conducting applied assessments for health and fitness within healthy populations.

title: Exercise and Wellness Across the Lifespan
description: Role of physical activity and exercise behavior in health and wellness. Personal applications plus gender and cultural implications of physical activity from childhood through adulthood.

title: Exercise and Nutrition for Health, Fitness, and Performance
description: Exercise, physical activity and nutrition information, guidelines, and misinformation. Effects of exercise and nutrition on disease prevention. Personal health, fitness, and performance goals.

title: Pathophysiology and Exercise Programming of Disease Populations I
description: Pathophysiology of musculoskeletal, neuromuscular, and cognitive/psychosocial disorders. Develop exercise programs through recommended guidelines.

title: Pathophysiology and Exercise Programming of Disease Populations II
description: Pathophysiology of pulmonary, cancer, and immune-related disorders. Develop exercise programs through recommended guidelines.

title: Program Design for Health, Fitness, and Performance
description: Theoretical and practical applications in cardiorespiratory and musculoskeletal exercise program design and corrective exercise. Laboratory includes implementing programs and coaching proper exercise form and technique.

title: Concepts in Metabolism and Weight Management
description: Overview of, and applications surrounding metabolism, weight management, and physiological/psycho-emotional/social considerations, dieting and body composition. Current and emerging trends and practices with related technology.

title: Exercise, Physical Activity, and Aging
description: Relationships between exercise, physical activity, and human aging including physiological, psychological, sociological, health and program considerations. Aging is viewed developmentally with emphasis on the middle and later years.

title: Promoting Physical Activity and Healthy Eating
description: Theoretical frameworks for integrating physical activity and nutrition in developing, implementing, and evaluating multicomponent interventions to increase these behaviors in a variety of population subgroups.

title: Adaptive Fitness Clinic
description: Hands-on experience working with individuals with a variety of physical and neurological disabilities through prescribed fitness programming at San Diego State University.

title: Community Rehabilitation Laboratory
description: Hands-on experience working with individuals with a variety of physical and neurological disabilities in the San Diego community.

title: Psychosocial Aspects of Disease and Injury Rehabilitation
description: Psychosocial factors related to disease and injury and effects on treatment and rehabilitation processes. Theoretical mechanisms through which psychosocial factors are affected by and influence disease, injury, and treatment and rehabilitation outcomes.

title: Instructional Leadership in Health and Clinical Settings
description: Andragogical and pedagogical theories, concepts, and techniques for enhancing instructional effectiveness and learning in exercise, physical activity, and rehabilitation settings.

title: Fitness Practitioner Internship
description: Supervised practical experience in developing and applying exercise programs and/or physical activity for apparently healthy persons and persons with clinical conditions in community, corporate, commercial, or medically supervised exercise settings.
notes: Only Kinesiology Fitness Specialist majors in their senior year may enroll. Students must contact Suzanne Meredith at smeredith@sdsu.edu for information on internship placement.  Enrollment entails participation in an on-campus or off-campus internship. Internships require a Service Learning Agreement with the internship site, which is facilitated by the instructor.   The following major is allowed:  KINESIOLOGY FITNESS SPECIALIST (556524)

title: Experimental Topics
description: Selected topics.
notes: See Class Schedule for specific content. Limit of nine units of any combination of 296, 496, 596 courses applicable to a bachelor’s degree.

title: Special Study
description: Individual study.

title: Selected Topics in Exercise and Nutritional Sciences
description: Selected topics in exercise and nutritional sciences.

title: Seminar in Kinesiology A
description: Seminar introducing current research in kinesiology through faculty and student presentations, journal article discussions, and peer review. Emphasizes critical analysis of scientific literature, scholarly dialogue, and development of academic presentation skills.

title: Seminar in Kinesiology B
description: Advanced seminar focused on development and presentation of original research in kinesiology, critical peer evaluation, and professional preparation. Includes career development topics such as grant writing, research statements, CV preparation, networking, and interview skills.

title: Experimental Methods in Exercise and Nutritional Sciences
description: Experimental methods in exercise and nutritional science.

title: Research Evaluation in Exercise and Nutritional Sciences
description: Techniques in designing, conducting, and reporting research in exercise and nutritional science. Qualitative and quantitative paradigms examined. Ethical consideration of human research.

title: Measurement and Evaluation in Exercise and Rehabilitation
description: Measurement theory and practice as applied to exercise and rehabilitation. Interpretation of measures used in physical medicine and rehabilitation contexts.

title: Evidence Based Practice in Athletic Training I
description: Clinically appraise best evidence to answer selected clinical questions; strategies for implementing evidence in daily practice. Holistic process for evaluating injuries and conditions common to physically active populations.

title: Evidence Based Practice in Athletic Training II
description: Critically appraise best evidence to answer selected clinical questions, and discuss strategies for implementing evidence into daily athletic training practice. Lower extremity injuries and conditions, therapeutic interventions, and general medical conditions.

title: Evidence Based Practice in Athletic Training III
description: Critically appraise best evidence to answer selected clinical questions, and discuss strategies for implementing evidence into daily athletic training practice. Upper extremity injuries and conditions, therapeutic interventions, pharmaceutical considerations, and psycho-social perspectives for the physically active.

title: Evidence Based Practice in Athletic Training IV
description: Critically appraise best evidence to answer selected clinical questions, and discuss strategies for implementing evidence into daily athletic training practice. Head, neck, and spine injuries and conditions, therapeutic interventions, and sports nutrition. Original collection (or treatment) of data leading to a research paper of scientific quality.

title: Professional Dissemination of Kinesiology Research
description: Pedagogy of scientific communication in kinesiology, with structured practice in writing, oral presentation, and data visualization. Emphasis on refining communication skills beyond research design and analysis, with application to scholarly, professional, and public audiences.

title: Biomechanics: Measurement Techniques I-Kinematics
description: Kinematic analysis of human movement using videography, electrogoniometry, and accelerometry with automated data reduction techniques typically used in study of pathomechanics.

title: Time Series Data Processing
description: Time-series data processing, signal filtering, data interpretation, data visualization, and a variety of science communication approaches as it relates to kinesiology.

title: Motor Control and Rehabilitation Science
description: Human movement in clinical and non-clinical populations using principles of motor control.

title: Pathopharmacology for Athletic Trainers
description: Foundational pharmacologic principles/topics, including drug actions and interactions, effects of various drug categories, and pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics. Examination of cellular aspects of the disease, pathophysiological signs/symptoms, and dynamics of body defenses related to health problems across the lifespan of physically active.
notes: Only open to students in the Master of Science in Athletic Training program.

title: Emergency Management of Sports Trauma
description: Recognition, management, and administration of appropriate emergency medical care to injured or ill athletes.

title: Clinical Anatomy
description: Structure and function of human musculoskeletal system. Palpation, primary muscle actions, muscle origins and insertions.

title: Prophylactic Interventions in Athletic Training Laboratory
description: Injury prevention through bracing, padding, taping, and wrapping techniques; managing and transporting injuries via ambulatory aids, spine boarding, splinting, and wrapping.

title: Introduction to Therapeutic Modalities
description:
Provides students with a comprehensive understanding of the principles, applications, and clinical significance of various therapeutic modalities. Explores theoretical foundations and
practical applications of therapeutic interventions aimed at preventing, managing, and rehabilitating musculoskeletal injuries commonly encountered in active populations.

title: Physiological Chemistry of Exercise
description: Biochemical and metabolic responses of the human body to acute and chronic exercise. Neuroendocrine control of fuel regulation during exercise.

title: Bio-Psychosocial Theories and Strategies in Athletic Training
description: Theory and research related to psychosocial aspects of injury and injury rehabilitation.

title: Psychosocial Aspects of Physical Activity
description: Explore the psychological and social influences affecting physical activity across the lifespan. Emphasis on examining the effects of physical activity on mental health and well-being, addressing disparities in physical activity participation, and designing evidence-based interventions in diverse populations.

title: Physical Activity Assessment
description: Comprehensive exploration of physical activity assessment methods, including evaluation and application of assessment tools in research and practice. Emphasizes practical skills for assessing physical activity across diverse populations and settings.

title: Professional Ethics, Management, Informatics, and Leadership in Athletic Training
description: Administrative aspects of athletic training. Contemporary guidelines of medical screening and documentation. Leadership theories and practices.

title: Professional Preparation in Athletic Training
description: Directed study for the board of certification for the athletic trainer examination through faculty-led review sessions.

title: Musculoskeletal Diagnostics for the Lower Extremity
description: Assessment principles and techniques for accurate diagnosis of injuries or conditions in physically active populations. Evidence-based approach to recognize, explain, and assess emergency medical situations, and conditions of lower extremity regions.

title: Musculoskeletal Diagnostics for the Lower Extremity Laboratory
description: Practical experience with assessment principles and techniques for accurate diagnosis of injuries or conditions in physically active populations. Evidence-based approach to recognize, explain, and assess emergency medical situations, and conditions of lower extremity regions.

title: Musculoskeletal Diagnostics for the Upper Extremity
description: Assessment principles and techniques for accurate diagnosis of injuries or conditions in physically active populations. Evidence-based approach to recognize, explain, and assess emergency medical situations, and conditions of upper extremity regions.

title: Musculoskeletal Diagnostics for the Upper Extremity Laboratory
description: Practical experience with assessment principles and techniques for accurate diagnosis of injuries or conditions in physically active populations. Evidence-based approach to recognize, explain, and assess emergency medical situations, and conditions of upper extremity regions.

title: Musculoskeletal Diagnostics for the Head and Spine
description: Assessment principles and techniques for accurate diagnosis of injuries or conditions in physically active populations. Evidence-based approach to recognize, explain, and assess emergency medical situations, and conditions of the head and spine regions.

title: Musculoskeletal Diagnostics for the Head and Spine Laboratory
description: Practical experience with assessment principles and techniques for accurate diagnosis of injuries or conditions in physically active populations. Evidence-based approach to recognize, explain, and assess emergency medical situations, and conditions of the head and spine regions.

title: Exercise Cardiology and Pathology
description: Interpretation of resting and exercise electrocardiograms with cardiopulmonary pathologies that skew interpretations.

title: Seminar in Advanced Physiology of Exercise
description: Advanced aspects of the physiology of exercise. Effects of exercise on human beings in relation to health, longevity, morphology and performance.

title: Advanced Exercise Physiology Laboratory
description: Laboratory course designed to develop competency in respiratory metabolism pulmonary function, gas analysis, blood chemistry and ergometry. Experience in the application of exercise procedures with human subjects and analysis and interpretation of results.

title: Musculoskeletal Interventions for the Lower Extremity
description: Physiological concepts and principles of comprehensive treatment and rehabilitation programs for managing athletic injuries and emergency medical situations of lower extremity regions.

title: Musculoskeletal Interventions for the Lower Extremity Laboratory
description: Practical experience with developing comprehensive treatment and rehabilitation programs for managing athletic injuries and emergency medical situations of lower extremity regions.

title: Musculoskeletal Interventions for the Upper Extremity
description: Physiological concepts and principles of comprehensive treatment and rehabilitation programs for managing athletic injuries and emergency medical situations of upper extremity regions.

title: Musculoskeletal Interventions for the Upper Extremity Laboratory
description: Practical experience with developing comprehensive treatment and rehabilitation programs for managing athletic injuries and emergency medical situations of upper extremity regions.

title: Musculoskeletal Interventions for the Head and Spine
description: Physiological concepts and principles of comprehensive treatment and rehabilitation programs for managing athletic injuries and emergency medical situations of head and spine regions.

title: Musculoskeletal Interventions for the Head and Spine Laboratory
description: Practical experience with developing comprehensive treatment and rehabilitation programs for managing athletic injuries and emergency medical situations of head and spine regions.

title: Adult Fitness: Exercise Prescription
description: Physical conditioning programs for the prevention, rehabilitation, and control of diseases associated with aging adults. Topics include disease etiology, health/disease evaluation, and exercise prescription for apparently healthy and diseased adults.

title: Athletic Training Clinical Internship I
description: Full immersion clinical internship in athletic training.

title: Athletic Training Clinical Internship II
description: Full immersion clinical internship in athletic training.

title: Advanced Topics in Exercise and Nutritional Sciences
description: Intensive study in specific areas of exercise and nutritional sciences.

title: Athletic Training Clinical Clerkship I
description: Cognitive, psychomotor, and affective skills of athletic training practice in a clinical setting. Competencies in emergency management, lower extremity, and lumbopelvic regions.

title: Athletic Training Clinical Clerkship II
description: Cognitive, psychomotor, and affective skills of athletic training practice in a clinical setting. Competencies in general medical conditions, upper extremity regions, and brachial plexus conditions.

title: Athletic Training Clinical Clerkship III
description: Cognitive, psychomotor, and affective skills of athletic training practice in a clinical setting. Competencies in bio-psychosocial strategies; and head, neck, and spine regions.

title: Athletic Training Clinical Clerkship IV
description: Cognitive, psychomotor, and affective skills of athletic training practice in a clinical setting. Competencies in nutrition, administration, informatics, and leadership.

title: Culminating Research Project
description: Preparation of a research project for the master’s degree.
notes: To take ENS 790, students MUST have been Advanced to Candidacy. Please see the ENS Graduate Advisor for permission to register for this class. Offered for credit/no credit only.

title: Exercise Science Internship
description: Supervised application of exercise laboratory testing, test interpretation, exercise prescription, and exercise leadership in adult fitness, corporate fitness, preventive medicine, and/or hospital disease rehabilitation settings.
notes: Three hours of laboratory per unit. This section has a zero-cost course materials (ZCCM) designation and exclusively uses digital course materials that are free of charge and may have an optional low-cost print version or there are no course materials required. The ZCCM designation may change if a new faculty member is assigned or other course materials are added.

title: Research
description: Three units of additional research under the supervision of a faculty member.
